model: Review upstream behavior and rewrite the required logic for the selected ESR; do not merge or cherry-pick upstream commits into the independent Embedder repository.

ports.intent: Select the desktop Remote Settings security/configuration collections through MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER without depending on a Firefox product name.
invariants: The decision is based on MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER, not MOZ_BUILD_APP == navis.
The security-state/intermediates collection remains selected.
A consumer with an unrelated build-project name receives the same desktop collection set.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's Remote Settings dump-selection code and express the same generic desktop predicate at its current selection point.

ports.intent: Link the Windows property-system library required by the retained Gecko accessibility implementation.
invariants: The dependency is Windows-only.
The dependency is present only when accessibility is compiled.
No Firefox frontend or installer dependency is introduced.
ports.port_review: First determine whether the target ESR already links propsys transitively or directly; retain this port only when the native accessibility link still requires it.

ports.intent: Enable Gecko's Windows launcher import-library tooling for a generic Desktop Embedder build without pretending the consumer is Firefox.
invariants: The hook is selected by MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER.
Non-Windows targets do not acquire the tool requirement.
The Firefox desktop-launcher product and installer remain outside the graph.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's launcher/toolchain checks and retain only the generic condition needed by the current WinLauncher integration.

ports.intent: Provide an upstream-default-on gate that removes the ONNX DOM/WebIDL, Toolkit ML, model provider, ONNX runtime, and native llama inference closure together.
invariants: Omitting --disable-local-ml preserves the selected ESR's normal behavior.
Disabling local ML removes native runtimes as well as WebIDL and product entry points.
Ordinary DOM, layout, networking, Fission, and sandbox behavior remain available.
ports.port_review: Inventory the target ESR's current local-inference entry points first; absent subsystems are inapplicable rather than code that should be recreated merely to gate them.

ports.intent: Define MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER and express the product-neutral Toolkit, DOM, IPC, services, Rust, packaging, startup graph, and absent-optional-service compatibility needed by the reusable desktop Runtime.
invariants: Runtime, Session, View, and Delegate source remains outside Gecko history.
Firefox Accounts, Sync, Firefox-only UI/services, DevTools product paths, and full Application Services aggregation stay outside the selected graph.
Fission, content-process launch, native sandboxing, networking, DOM, layout, graphics, storage, and security remain Gecko responsibilities.
No predicate depends on the Navis product name.
Legacy Toolkit callers tolerate deliberately absent XPI, updater timer, and js-ctypes services without startup or shutdown errors.
A target-ESR port preserves the public source API rather than exposing target-specific Gecko objects.
ports.port_review: This is the primary semantic port. Rebuild its decisions against the target ESR's current graph and APIs; do not treat failed textual application as a merge conflict to be solved mechanically.

ports.intent: Remove the browser WebExtensions/XPI runtime while retaining the smaller URI-policy and StreamFilter substrate consumed by Gecko core.
invariants: The extension installation, XPIProvider, content-script, browser API, actor, schema, and product UI closure is absent when disabled.
Core extension policy and Necko StreamFilter behavior required by Gecko remains.
Service Worker and worker WebIDL changes are gated as one coherent runtime boundary.
Omitting --disable-webextensions-runtime preserves upstream behavior.
ports.port_review: Review WebIDL, worker, AddonManager, actor, packaging, and legacy InstallTrigger integration on the target ESR and port the capability boundary logically.

ports.intent: Make the residual SDP Rust bridge follow Gecko's existing WebRTC feature so a no-WebRTC profile actually removes it from gkrust.
invariants: The default WebRTC profile retains the SDP bridge.
A MOZ_WEBRTC=false build has no rsdparsa_capi source in the final gkrust dependency closure.
The fake/shared non-WebRTC media substrate remains independently classified.
ports.port_review: Inspect the target ESR's gkrust feature graph and gate whichever current SDP bridge creates the equivalent unconditional edge.

ports.intent: Provide a desktop-embedder-only gate that removes the Glean/FOG, DAP, Gecko Trace, generated metrics, and firefox-on-glean Rust closure while preserving required Gecko call surfaces through inert compatibility facades.
invariants: Omitting --disable-observability-runtime preserves the selected ESR's normal Glean/FOG, DAP, and Gecko Trace integrations.
A disabled build has no firefox-on-glean or generated Glean metric source in the linked gkrust dependency closure.
Window and privileged-JS Glean compatibility surfaces remain inert so retained Gecko modules do not need product-specific rewrites.
Fission IPC, HTTP/3, WebRender, WebGPU, security storage, and retained media behavior remain functional.
This gate does not claim to remove Gecko's separate legacy Telemetry core.
ports.port_review: Inventory current Glean consumers and Rust feature-unification edges on the target ESR, then preserve only compatibility surfaces required by retained engine code; review legacy Telemetry separately.

ports.intent: Link the platform-neutral Navis Core lifecycle state and its narrow C ABI into libxul only for a Desktop Embedder build.
invariants: Runtime, Session, and View lifecycle rules remain in the Gecko-independent navis-core crate.
The Gecko dependency is a private FFI edge selected only by MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER.
No Gecko object, XPCOM type, UI type, or operating-system type enters the shared Rust crate.
WebGPU and the retained Gecko web engine remain unaffected by the control-core link.
ports.port_review: Re-evaluate the target ESR's gkrust aggregation point, link the same narrow FFI crate under its generic embedder build predicate, and regenerate the target Cargo lockfile without importing platform logic into navis-core.

ports.intent: Extend the disabled observability profile across legacy Telemetry by removing its collectors, stores, archive, startup controller, pings, pingsender, diagnostic UI, and dedicated collection services while retaining a constant-off ABI/process-clock facade.
invariants: Omitting --disable-observability-runtime preserves the selected ESR's normal legacy Telemetry implementation and product modules.
A disabled build cannot enable recording and has no event, scalar, histogram, I/O, memory, untrusted-module, archive, or submission store.
The nsITelemetry compatibility service retains only empty/no-op methods and the process-clock behavior required by retained Gecko code.
Remote Settings keeps its validation/status contract but performs no uptake recording.
Extension startup does not import the removed TelemetrySession solely to annotate crash-report add-on state.
No pingsender executable, background task, Telemetry startup component, about:telemetry/about:glean UI, or dedicated idle collector enters the runtime.
ports.port_review: Inventory the target ESR's legacy Telemetry build, startup registrations, pingsender paths, diagnostic pages, dedicated collectors, and non-recording API consumers; rebuild a constant-off compatibility surface only for callers that remain in the selected Core graph.

ports.intent: Give every Desktop Embedder consumer a fail-closed application-extension allowlist so a product can host multiple reviewed built-ins without starting arbitrary files copied beside the executable.
invariants: Only MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER consumers change application-global enumeration semantics.
The allowlist accepts a collection of extension IDs and does not assume any product or extension identity.
An empty or missing locked allowlist starts no application-global extension.
Allowlisted application packages use non-sideloaded built-in lifecycle semantics but still require normal AMO signature verification.
Every non-application install location retains its upstream behavior.
ports.port_review: Locate the target ESR's application-global XPI enumeration boundary and re-express the generic Desktop Embedder ID filter before unregistered add-ons enter startup state; do not weaken signature verification or change other products.

ports.intent: Retain the WebExtensions execution paths needed by reviewed application built-ins while keeping public installation, Add-ons Manager, the unused extension-based default theme, autonomous extension updates and native-messaging implementations outside every Desktop Embedder product.
invariants: Application-owned XPI lifecycle, content scripts, extension storage, webRequest and ordinary browser APIs remain available.
Desktop Embedder packages contain no Add-ons Manager content or skin and register no Web install content handler or extension update timer.
Desktop Embedder XPI startup does not attempt to install Gecko's extension-based default theme when that resource is deliberately absent.
Desktop Embedder builds contain no native-messaging host discovery module, bridge component or portal interface.
storage.managed reports the ordinary no-managed-manifest result without importing native-host discovery in Desktop Embedder products.
Firefox, Android and other non-Desktop-Embedder products retain their upstream extension surfaces.
ports.port_review: Re-audit the target ESR's Add-ons Manager resources, install entry points, update timer categories and native-messaging source/registration graph; preserve the bounded built-in execution closure without restoring product-facing management surfaces.

ports.intent: Retain Gecko's loopback WebDriver BiDi and Marionette content-automation paths for deterministic testing while preventing Desktop Embedder automation from becoming a privileged or extension-installation side channel.
invariants: WebDriver remains dormant unless an explicit automation flag is supplied and its Gecko listeners stay loopback-only.
Desktop Embedder cannot enable parent-process system access through either the command line or environment.
Marionette exposes no Addon:Install, Addon:Uninstall or chrome-context switch command in a Desktop Embedder package.
WebDriver BiDi exposes no webExtension module and packages neither its extension mutation module nor the shared Addon helper.
Desktop Embedder sessions are projected through the reusable tab registry so WebDriver discovers, creates, activates and closes content contexts without reaching into product UI code.
The Desktop Embedder tab adapter forwards frame-loader event observation to its owning chrome window so Marionette can track process switches without Firefox gBrowser.
Desktop Embedder automation exposes only the product's default user context and does not restore the excluded container-identity service.
The minimal devtools/platform SpiderMonkey Debugger bridge required by WebDriver script realms is retained without the DevTools client, server, shared framework or startup integration.
Navigation, content DOM/JavaScript, input, network observation, screenshots and lifecycle commands remain available.
Firefox and other non-Desktop-Embedder products retain their upstream WebDriver extension and privileged-debug behavior.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's Remote Agent, TabManager, Marionette command registry and WebDriver BiDi module registry/package manifests; rebind changed tab/window call sites to the reusable Desktop Embedder registry, remove every current extension mutation entry point and permanently deny parent-process access only for MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER while preserving content automation.

ports.intent: Define upstream-default-on gates for EME, Web Push and Safe Browsing, then remove Navis 1.0's encrypted-media Web surface, concrete CDM packages and GMP product distribution/update runtime while retaining internal media ABI/adapter/process substrate required by ordinary Gecko playback.
invariants: Omitting the new disable options preserves the selected ESR's normal EME, Web Push and Safe Browsing selections.
A MOZ_EME_API=false build exposes neither Navigator.requestMediaKeySystemAccess nor HTMLMediaElement encrypted-media members and events.
No ClearKey implementation, fake CDM or concrete CDM binary enters the disabled build or product package.
When both EME and WebRTC are disabled, no GMP provider, update manager or OpenH264/Widevine distribution descriptor enters the product package.
Generic Chromium CDM interfaces, adapter compatibility code, host types and GMP process substrate may remain only as inert internal dependencies of retained Gecko media code.
The Web Push and Safe Browsing controls are consumed by their following semantic ports rather than by product-name predicates.
ports.port_review: Inventory the target ESR's EME WebIDL entry points, concrete CDM implementations, media build graph and internal CDM type consumers; rebuild the public capability cut without deleting shared ABI types that retained non-EME media still compiles against. Re-evaluate the Web Push and Safe Browsing control declarations together with their dedicated following ports.

ports.intent: Remove the Web Push WebIDL surface, DOM runtime, service-worker integration and content-process messaging together when MOZ_WEB_PUSH is disabled, while preserving ordinary Service Workers.
invariants: Omitting --disable-web-push preserves the selected ESR's normal Push API and runtime behavior.
A disabled build exposes no PushManager, PushEvent, PushMessageData, PushSubscription or push event handler to Web content.
The dom/push runtime, Push IPC operations, quota notification and service-worker push dispatch do not enter the selected graph.
Legacy nsIPush declarations may remain as inert ABI, but retained service-worker manager calls fail with NS_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE.
Service Worker registration, fetch and lifecycle behavior unrelated to Push remain available.
ports.port_review: Inventory the target ESR's Push WebIDL, DOM directory, service-worker operations, IPDL, permission mapping, notification quota and legacy XPIDL consumers; remove the executable/runtime closure while retaining only compatibility declarations still required by ordinary Service Workers.

ports.intent: Remove Safe Browsing providers, application-reputation services, list-update modules, diagnostic UI and provider configuration together while retaining generic URL-classifier substrate shared by other privacy capabilities.
invariants: Omitting --disable-safe-browsing preserves the selected ESR's normal provider and reputation behavior.
A disabled build has no application-reputation implementation, component registration, SafeBrowsing/ListManager/HashCompleter module, about:url-classifier page or provider/table endpoint preferences.
The provider XPIDL is absent; retained generic downloads use a gated local copy of the stable verdict values only when the provider interface is unavailable.
Generic URL-classifier database and classification infrastructure remain available to independently retained tracking-protection features.
Downloads with a nonempty extension conservatively require confirmation when no application-reputation provider exists.
No product-name predicate or replacement network provider is introduced.
ports.port_review: Inventory the target ESR's URL-classifier provider modules, application-reputation interface and implementation, Remote Settings/list updaters, diagnostic pages, download decision paths and preferences; remove provider-backed behavior without conflating it with generic classifier consumers, and verify the provider-free verdict fallback against the target interface values.

ports.intent: Add an upstream-default-off geolocation policy that selects only operating-system providers and turns every Linux GeoClue/XDG Portal network-fallback path into the standard unavailable result.
invariants: Omitting the native-only preference preserves the selected ESR's normal provider selection, test override and network fallback behavior.
A native-only build or product never selects the direct network geolocation provider, including when the Gecko test-provider preference is set.
GeoClue errors and timeouts and XDG Portal startup errors and timeouts cannot instantiate MLSFallback's network provider under the policy.
Successful Linux GeoClue/XDG Portal, Windows Location and macOS CoreLocation paths remain unchanged.
An absent, failed or nonresponsive native provider reports the standard POSITION_UNAVAILABLE result instead of silently querying a remote endpoint.
ports.port_review: Inventory the target ESR's platform-provider selection and every direct, error and timeout network-fallback edge; re-express the default-off policy at those current boundaries and verify both native success and provider-unavailable behavior with deterministic platform-service doubles.

ports.intent: Keep Gecko's native GTest runner usable when the observability runtime is disabled by gating FOG/DAP initialization, tests and Rust dependencies behind the same build selection.
invariants: An observability-enabled build retains the upstream FOG and DAP GTest crates, test directories and early FOG initialization.
An observability-disabled build links neither fog-gtest nor dap_ffi-gtest into gkrust-gtest.
The generic GTest runner and unrelated native test suites remain available in the production capability profile.
This port changes test infrastructure only and does not reintroduce a product observability implementation.
ports.port_review: Inspect the target ESR's native test runner initialization, telemetry test directories and gkrust-gtest dependency graph; apply the existing observability selection consistently without hiding unrelated tests.

ports.intent: Expose the current PermissionsPolicy API and structured Permissions-Policy header semantics, preserve container/header inheritance across process boundaries and enforce the sync-xhr policy-controlled feature.
invariants: Content exposes document.permissionsPolicy and iframe.permissionsPolicy but not the obsolete featurePolicy aliases.
The structured Permissions-Policy header accepts self, wildcard, scheme, host and port source expressions and ignores the obsolete Feature-Policy response header.
Header policy, iframe allow policy, nested inheritance, sandboxed opaque origins and cross-process container policy compose without granting a feature denied by an ancestor.
Synchronous XHR is advertised with a default-all allowlist and throws NetworkError from send() when policy disables it.
The selected WPT metadata records no expected failures for behavior covered by this port.
ports.port_review: Reconcile the target ESR's Permissions Policy WebIDL, parser, inheritance and cross-process container representation with the current structured-header and introspection algorithms; rerun the selected upstream WPT matrix and native parser tests before accepting the port.

ports.intent: Let explicit --enable-tests Desktop Embedder builds use Gecko's WPT preference harness while production packages retain content-only WebDriver and no extension-installation side door.
invariants: Desktop Embedder production builds continue to reject parent-process system access even when the command-line flag or environment variable is supplied.
Only an ENABLE_TESTS build with the explicit upstream system-access opt-in can enter chrome context for Gecko-owned harness setup.
Marionette retains SetContext so content-only automation works; requesting chrome context still requires system access.
The WPT mach command recognizes a generic Desktop Embedder build without making the product pretend to be Firefox.
Test-only managed extension storage is ignored in every production build and may only provide deterministic policy to reviewed application built-ins in an ENABLE_TESTS build.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's Remote Agent access decision, Marionette context command, WPT product predicate and managed-storage entry point; preserve the compile-time production/test distinction and verify both positive test-harness access and negative production access.

ports.intent: Remove the inert print and legacy InstallTrigger globals from Desktop Embedder Web content when their corresponding product capabilities and executable implementations are excluded.
invariants: A build with NS_PRINTING=false does not expose window.print to content.
A MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER build does not expose the legacy InstallTrigger compatibility global.
Desktop Embedder retains the reviewed application-built-in WebExtensions execution path without exposing a Web installation entry point.
Printing-enabled products and non-Desktop-Embedder products retain their upstream Window surfaces.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's Window WebIDL for printing and legacy extension-installation compatibility surfaces; keep each public member conditional on the executable product capability rather than inheriting an inert content-visible stub.

ports.intent: Keep Web-platform and engine-recovery about documents while making Firefox product about pages unreachable in a Desktop Embedder build that exposes its own internal-page protocol.
invariants: about:blank and the unresolvable about:srcdoc engine token retain their selected-ESR semantics.
Network, certificate, HTTPS-only and subframe-crash error documents remain available as engine-private recovery surfaces.
Every other registered Firefox product or diagnostic about module fails closed before channel creation in a Desktop Embedder build.
Unknown or excluded about names retain dangerous protocol flags and cannot become content-linkable aliases.
Non-Desktop-Embedder products retain the selected ESR's complete about namespace.
ports.port_review: Inventory the target ESR's standards-required about semantics and engine-owned error/recovery documents, then reconstruct the minimum central allowlist without re-exposing target product pages or bypassing the target protocol security checks.

ports.intent: Construct only the Desktop Embedder navis scheme as a standard authority URI so exact registered pages receive stable content principals without making the scheme web-loadable.
invariants: Only a Desktop Embedder product that supplies MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER_INTERNAL_SCHEME receives the standard-URI branch; other products and unknown schemes retain upstream behavior.
The product-selected internal scheme uses standard authority parsing, enabling a stable content principal tied to the exact scheme, host and route.
The protocol remains URI_DANGEROUS_TO_LOAD and has no DNS, network or search fallback.
Malformed or unknown page resolution still fails closed in the Navis handler before channel creation.
Identity still requires handler resolution plus exact document and principal route equality; URL text alone is insufficient.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's unknown-scheme URI construction and retain the smallest Navis-only standard-URI branch; re-run principal, framing and spoofing, malformed-route and non-Desktop-Embedder regression gates.

ports.intent: Retain the minimal static certificate-decoding dependency closure used by Gecko error documents while keeping the Firefox certificate-viewer frontend, actors and tests outside Desktop Embedder products.
invariants: Desktop Embedder packages certDecoder.mjs, its two local data/helper modules and its pinned PKI parser dependency as inert data-decoding support.
No Firefox certificate-viewer HTML, CSS, component UI, parent actor, child actor or product page enters the selected graph.
Gecko network and certificate error documents can decode bounded failed-certificate facts without a missing chrome resource.
Navis certificate details remain a Platform-owned Material surface populated only from immutable Core projections.
Non-Desktop-Embedder products retain the selected ESR's complete certificate-viewer directory and tests.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's aboutNetError certificate imports and certificate-viewer dependency graph; retain only the minimal decoder closure required by engine errors and re-audit the package for frontend pages, actors and styles.

ports.intent: Register Gecko's certificate-error document in the shared engine about redirector for Desktop Embedder products whose application graph does not include Firefox's browser redirector.
invariants: Only MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER adds the certerror contract to the shared docshell redirector; Firefox and other products retain their existing registration owner.
about:certerror resolves to Gecko's engine error document with the same safe-content, child-process, script and hidden flags as the selected Firefox implementation.
The route remains engine-private under the central Desktop Embedder about allowlist and is never advertised as a public Navis internal page.
Invalid certificates fail closed into a visible error document while the omnibox retains the failed HTTPS URL.
No Firefox certificate-viewer page, browser AboutRedirector or other browser product page enters the Desktop Embedder graph.
ports.port_review: Compare the target ESR's owner and flags for about:certerror with the shared docshell redirector; keep one non-conflicting Desktop Embedder registration and replay trusted and untrusted local TLS fixtures.

ports.intent: Synchronize GTK's native fallback focus with the IM context when a Desktop Embedder chrome document activates before its remote view has selected a DOM focus target.
invariants: A Desktop Embedder GTK toplevel that takes the native focus before selecting a DOM target records the same nsWindow as the IM context dispatch target.
Later editable remote-content focus can enable IBus and dispatch compositionstart, compositionupdate, compositionend, beforeinput and input through Gecko's native IME path.
Native preedit cancellation does not commit text and leaves the editable value unchanged.
The change is gated by MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER; Firefox and other products retain the selected ESR's upstream GTK focus fallback.
The regression gate uses real IBus/libpinyin and AT-SPI keyboard synthesis rather than DOM event injection or a privileged WebDriver context.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's GTK focus-in fallback and IMContextWrapper ownership contract; preserve the smallest Desktop Embedder-only synchronization point and replay native IBus commit and cancellation paths.

ports.intent: Dismiss Gecko-owned Select and date/time picker popups when content scroll or viewport resizing invalidates their screen-space anchor.
invariants: Select and date/time controls retain Gecko's value, focus, event, keyboard and accessibility semantics.
A content scroll captured from the document or a nested scroll container closes the open popup when the control's screen-space anchor moves instead of leaving the popup detached.
A queued scroll event that completed before the picker opened does not immediately close a correctly anchored popup.
A trusted pointer press in content outside the owning input closes an open date/time picker before the unrelated control action continues.
A content viewport resize closes the popup before its opening rectangle becomes stale.
Navigation and explicit-close behavior remain owned by the existing child actors, and closing remains idempotent across parent acknowledgement.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's Select child and common input-picker actor lifecycles; attach dismissal at their current content-side anchor owner and replay document scroll, nested scroll, resize, keyboard commit and pagehide behavior.

ports.intent: Translate Gecko-owned Date/Time picker and media-control presentation toward the frozen Chromium 152 desktop reference without replacing trusted control implementations.
invariants: Gecko continues to own form value, event, focus, keyboard, accessibility and media behavior; no content or Platform overlay emulates a native control.
Select keeps the existing trusted XUL popup because its Linux density, anchor and option presentation already match the pinned Chrome reference within the accepted tolerance.
Date/Time geometry and states follow the observed Chromium 152 calendar and list-picker density while retaining locale, range, step and high-contrast behavior.
Video uses a bottom gradient, 32-pixel actions and a 4-pixel track; audio uses a system-color capsule while the retained Gecko media state machine stays unchanged.
The translation is based on Chromium tag 152.0.7977.64 resources and must be visually re-evaluated rather than blindly carried across either upstream tree.
ports.port_review: Compare the target ESR's trusted picker documents and UA media shadow controls with Chromium 152's calendar_picker.css, list_picker.css and mediaControls.css; rewrite only presentation values and replay native open, scroll-dismiss, keyboard commit, media interaction, accessibility, theme and scale tests.

ports.intent: Let a Desktop Embedder declare an exact Remote Settings collection allowlist that governs packaged bootstrap dumps, polling, explicit client reads and synchronization without weakening Gecko content-signature verification.
invariants: Omitting the allowlist preserves upstream and generic Desktop Embedder behavior; a nonempty list is valid only in Desktop Embedder mode and must be sorted and unique.
The same bucket/collection identifiers filter generated dump timestamps, packaged JSON and attachment payloads, central polling and explicit RemoteSettings clients.
A disallowed client returns no records and performs no synchronization even when an old profile database exists.
Production preview bucket names normalize to their reviewed base bucket; preview mode remains unavailable through Navis's locked production preferences.
Test builds bypass the product allowlist by default so upstream arbitrary-collection and invalid-signature tests retain their original coverage, while a dedicated test can force the policy boundary.
Collection signature verification, signer identities, rollback behavior and the Mozilla production endpoint remain Gecko-owned and unchanged.
ports.port_review: Inventory the target ESR's dump installers, timestamp generator, startup bundle, polling/client factory and signature tests; reapply one generic allowlist at every current package and synchronization boundary, then replay both the forced policy test and the upstream invalid-signature suite.

ports.intent: Let a generic Desktop Embedder present Gecko's validated related-origin WebAuthn consent through its own bounded prompt contract while preserving Firefox PopupNotifications and Android GeckoView behavior.
invariants: The related-origin well-known fetch, origin-list validation and WebAuthn transaction remain Gecko-owned and unchanged.

A Desktop Embedder receives only the requesting browsing-context identity, authenticated origin, RP ID and create/use mode; its product layer never receives the fetch callback or Gecko manager object.
Missing, throwing, rejected, malformed, navigated-away and canceled embedder decisions fail closed as user cancellation.
Firefox continues to use PopupNotifications, Android continues to use GeckoViewPrompter, and embedders without the hook retain the selected ESR behavior.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's WebAuthnRelatedOriginFetcher desktop presentation point and retain a fail-closed generic browser-element hook before the Firefox PopupNotifications fallback; replay valid, denied, rejected, navigation-canceled and malformed related-origin flows.

ports.intent: Install the generated built-in dictionary registry in a product-neutral Desktop Embedder resource location and make the shared XPI provider load it there so packaged Hunspell dictionaries become usable editor capabilities rather than inert bytes.
invariants: Desktop Embedder builds package exactly one generated registry under resource://gre/modules so both unpacked trees and packaged OmniJars can resolve it alongside the resource://gre dictionary payloads.
Only the Desktop Embedder registry URI changes; Firefox, Android, Thunderbird and other Gecko products retain their selected-ESR locations and behavior.
The generated registry, rather than a Navis-specific hard-coded dictionary identity, remains the authority for built-in dictionary registration.
Missing or invalid registry data fails closed without restoring public dictionary installation or extension-management surfaces.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's built_in_addons generation, installation destinations and XPIProvider startup URI; retain a generic Desktop Embedder resource destination and prove both packaged dictionary bytes and live editor suggestions.

ports.intent: Route WebAuthn transactions to a registered WebDriver virtual authenticator without changing a product's locked native-authenticator preferences or exposing the software token to content.
invariants: Only the existing privileged WebDriver/XPCOM virtual-authenticator commands can create the routing condition; Web content cannot register or discover a test token.

While at least one virtual authenticator exists, registration, assertion, UVPAA and conditional-autofill discovery use the virtual-token manager; removing the last authenticator immediately restores the configured production route.
Production soft-token and USB-token preferences remain unchanged and may stay locked; a normal browser session continues to use native authenticators only.
Virtual authenticator consent is governed by the WebDriver isUserConsenting and isUserVerified state, while real USB operations retain the native presence prompt and all existing PIN/device flows.
The port changes no WebAuthn DOM API, credential serialization, relying-party validation or non-desktop platform service selection.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's WebDriver virtual-authenticator service entry points and authrs transport selection; preserve privileged registration as the sole activation signal, route all virtual registration/assertion/autofill capability paths consistently, and replay both virtual automation and native USB-policy gates.

ports.intent: Build Gecko's Windows notification COM activation server for a generic Desktop Embedder so native notifications remain actionable after the browser process exits.
invariants: The notification activation server is selected only on Windows for Firefox, Thunderbird or a generic Desktop Embedder build.
The predicate depends on MOZ_DESKTOP_EMBEDDER rather than a Navis product name.
Linux, macOS, Android and unrelated non-desktop products do not acquire the Windows COM server.
The port changes no Web Notification DOM surface, permission semantics, toast content or provider selection.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's Windows notification-server configure gate and keep the generic Desktop Embedder predicate only if portable native notification activation still depends on the same COM server.

ports.intent: Enforce Gecko's adjusted WebAuthn ceremony lifetime around the Windows native provider because the operating-system timeout is documented as guidance and may be overridden by the platform.
invariants: The timer uses the already adjusted WebAuthn timeout and is bound to the exact Gecko transaction ID.
Expiry reaches the existing Windows cancellation GUID and native WebAuthNCancelCurrentOperation path before the DOM promise rejects with NotAllowedError.
Success, user cancellation, AbortSignal cancellation and transaction replacement cancel the timer, while an expired timer cannot cancel a later transaction.
The correction changes only the Windows native WebAuthn provider and does not enable a software authenticator or alter virtual-authenticator routing.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's Windows WebAuthn provider and retain an exact-transaction client lifetime timer whenever the native dwTimeoutMilliseconds remains advisory; prove natural no-device termination, AbortSignal cancellation and subsequent-transaction isolation.

ports.intent: Route standards WebDriver virtual-authenticator ceremonies through Gecko's authenticator-rs test-token manager even when a native platform provider is available and the product's software-token preference is locked off.
invariants: Only successfully created privileged virtual-authenticator IDs enter the top-level WebAuthn service's active set.
While that set is nonempty, registration, assertion and conditional credential discovery use authenticator-rs on Windows, macOS and other native-provider platforms.
Successful removal deletes the exact ID, and removing the last virtual authenticator restores the native production provider for later ceremonies.
The route does not unlock the software-token preference, expose authenticator IDs to Web content or create a production software fallback.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's WebAuthn service selection and WebDriver virtual-authenticator implementation; retain explicit active-ID routing whenever virtual commands and content ceremonies otherwise select different services on native-provider platforms.

ports.intent: Dismiss Gecko-owned Select and date/time picker popups when content removes the DOM element that owns their screen-space anchor.
invariants: The document-subtree observer exists only while the native picker is open and disconnects on every normal close path.
Removing the exact owning Select or date/time input closes the parent popup instead of leaving an orphaned native surface.
Unrelated content mutations do not close or rebuild the picker while its owner remains connected.
Navigation remains covered by the existing pagehide path, and scroll, resize, outside-pointer, value, focus, keyboard and accessibility behavior remain unchanged.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's Select child and common input-picker lifetime ownership; preserve a bounded open-only disconnection observer if removing the anchor does not otherwise generate the actor's close signal, then replay removal, pagehide and ordinary commit paths.

ports.intent: Prevent an obsolete WebDriver WindowRealm from disabling automation features on the new global to which its WindowProxy was retargeted during navigation.
invariants: Each WindowRealm captures the inner-window identity of the global for which its automation features were enabled.
Destroying a realm disables async-stack and unlimited-stack capture only while that same inner window remains the current global.
Tab removal, same-origin navigation and cross-origin navigation cannot make obsolete-realm cleanup touch the replacement global or emit a chrome://remote Realm error.
Normal cleanup of a live current global remains intact, and the production content-only WebDriver boundary does not regain add-on installation or another privileged product surface.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's WindowRealm ownership and navigation teardown ordering; retain inner-window identity validation while Window remains a retargetable WindowProxy, then replay tab removal plus same-origin and cross-origin navigation with automation features enabled.

ports.intent: Keep the active profile extension location available for explicit Navis manager installs while preventing copied files and foreign directory scans from becoming an alternate installation entry point.

Application-owned built-ins continue to be discovered only through their immutable registry and application location.
Automation may select explicit side-load scopes for isolated upstream and product tests without changing the production constant.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's XPI location and side-load policy split; preserve the distinction between direct AddonManager installation and directory discovery, then replay copied-file rejection, manager install and restart persistence.

ports.intent: Retain managed-extension inventory and events while preventing the generic WebExtensions management namespace from becoming an alternate install, removal or state-mutation path around navis://extensions/.

ports.intent: Give the engine-owned network, certificate, HTTPS-only and subframe-crash recovery documents one opt-in Material presentation without replacing their Gecko loading and recovery semantics.
invariants: The presentation is inactive unless the consuming desktop product explicitly enables its preference; other Gecko products retain the selected ESR appearance.

Network and DNS failures, TLS and certificate failures, HTTPS-only interstitials and subframe crashes keep their original document channels, failed-URL identity, retry, back, exception and diagnostic behavior.
The retained error family shares responsive Material typography, controls, surfaces and focus states in light, dark, reduced-motion and forced-color environments.
Firefox/Mozilla support links remain absent unless the consuming product deliberately enables an owned error-help destination.

ports.port_review: Inventory the target ESR's engine-owned error and recovery documents, identify both legacy and custom-element render paths, and translate presentation only after preserving every action, security delay, accessibility state and private error URI.

ports.intent: Let a Gecko embedder supply one trusted local query-stripping policy to navigation and copy/share consumers, with explicit registrable-domain scope and an opt-out from the default Remote Settings adapter.
invariants: The new product policy URI is optional, accepts only chrome or resource schemes, validates a bounded versioned envelope and leaves upstream products unchanged when absent.
Global, exact-host, registrable-domain and allow-domain rules are normalized into one fresh projection; removed provider entries cannot remain through mutation of a cached base list.
The unified consumer path is default-off and must be explicitly enabled by a product, while legacy Gecko query stripping retains its selected-ESR behavior otherwise.
A product may disable the query-stripping Remote Settings client without disabling unrelated Remote Settings infrastructure or weakening content-signature validation for retained collections.
Registrable-domain matching uses Gecko's effective-TLD service; it does not reinterpret exact-host origins as suffix wildcards or apply a scoped parameter globally.
ports.port_review: Review the target ESR's query-stripping list service, Strip-on-Share rule dictionary, navigation stripper and Remote Settings initialization; preserve opt-in product policy and unified-consumer gates, then replay global, exact-host, registrable-domain, allow-domain, offline-first and provider-update replacement cases.
